public_prompt: Every deployment is recorded as successful, including one that never reached the target and left the previous version live. The reading so far: find the defect in the pipeline step and repair it. Name the defect and give the repair.
observable_resources: ci/deploy.sh — the step is `deploy_cmd | tee deploy.log`, with no pipefail setting
ci/run-1841.log — deploy_cmd printed 'authentication failed' and the step was recorded green
ci/exit-codes.md — 41 of the last 300 runs hold an error line in deploy.log and are recorded green
ops/version-audit.csv — for 6 of those 41 the target version never moved
closure:deploy-frequency-target — closed; commits to daily production deploys; rests on the delivery plan, not on how a step reports its result
closure:deploy-approval-gate — closed; requires two approvals before a production deploy; rests on the change standard, not on how the step reports its result
closure:rollback-runbook — closed; documents how to revert a bad version; rests on the operations standard, not on this reporting defect
closure:deploy-notification-channel — closed; fixes where deploy outcomes are announced; rests on the communications standard, not on how the step decides its result

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the answer names the unset pipefail — the failing command's status being discarded by the pipe — as the defect, repairs the step, and re-checks the 41 affected runs. The pipeline's structure must be left untouched. FAIL if the answer proposes scraping logs for error strings as the primary repair, redesigns the pipeline, or concludes the deployments genuinely succeeded.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: Run defect: a pipe discards the deploy command's exit status. The pipeline design is correct; setting pipefail resolves it. Reframing is the wrong move.
